headline: Bonsai 27B runs on a phone, the first 27B-class model to do so
summary: Bonsai 27B, a new multimodal flagship based on Qwen3.6 27B, is the first 27B-class model to run on a phone, achieving this feat by using 1-bit and ternary weights for a footprint as small as 3.9 GB.
details: Bonsai 27B, based on Qwen3.6 27B, is the new multimodal flagship model, now capable of running on a phone. This 27B-class model offers advanced multi-step reasoning, structured tool calls, and vision tasks.

Previously, deploying such a model locally was impractical; a 27B model needs 54GB in 16-bit precision or 18GB even in a 4-bit build. Bonsai 27B overcomes this with ternary {−1, 0, +1} weights for a 5.9 GB 'quality' variant, and 1-bit {−1, +1} weights for a 3.9 GB 'footprint' variant.

The 1-bit Bonsai 27B, at 3.9 GB, fits within the memory budget of an iPhone 17 Pro, making it the first 27B-class model on a phone. Both variants are multimodal, including a compact 4-bit vision tower for processing screenshots, documents, and camera input.

Across 15 benchmarks, Ternary Bonsai 27B retains 95% of full-precision baseline performance, while 1-bit Bonsai 27B retains 90%. Key capabilities like math, coding, and tool calling remain nearly untouched, crucial for agentic workloads.

This represents a significant Pareto shift, delivering 27B-class capability at a footprint smaller than a full-precision 2B model. The 1-bit Bonsai 27B achieves 0.53 intelligence density per GB, over 10x the full-precision baseline.

AI workloads are evolving from single responses to sustained, agentic work, involving hundreds of model calls. Cloud-only execution imposes structural constraints, with accumulating costs and privacy concerns as data crosses networks.

Local execution changes this, allowing agents to live inside the product with zero marginal cost for multi-step loops and ensuring user data stays on-device. This unlocks new categories like persistent on-device agents and offline assistants.

Bonsai 27B provides the necessary capability and small footprint for these local deployments. It also enables hybrid architectures, routing non-frontier tasks locally and reserving cloud models for the hardest steps, collapsing overall system costs.

The model supports a full 262K-token context and speculative decoding for speed. It reaches up to 163 tokens/second in its 1-bit variant, and everything is available today under the Apache 2.0 License.

headline_marked: [[Hinge founder raised $18M for new AI dating service]], Overtone
headline: Hinge founder raised $18M for new AI dating service, Overtone
summary: Overtone, a voice- and audio-forward service, uses AI for highly curated introductions, moving away from traditional profiles and swiping to combat dating app burnout. It secured $18M in funding.
details: Justin McLeod, founder of popular dating app Hinge, has announced an $18 million fundraise for his new venture, Overtone. Investors include Hinge owner Match Group, along with FirstMark Capital and Pace Capital.

Overtone describes itself as a "voice- and audio-forward service, enabled by AI, that provides highly curated introductions." McLeod stated it's "not a dating app" in the traditional sense, avoiding profiles, algorithmic feeds, and the endless cycle of likes and matches.

This new approach aims to address widespread user dissatisfaction and burnout with current dating apps. A 2024 Forbes Health survey found that 78% of dating app users felt burnt out, spending significant time without finding fulfilling connections.

Unlike many apps using AI for conversation starters or profile building, Overtone focuses on using AI to deeply understand individuals through their own voice and stories. The goal is to make only meaningful introductions, transparently explaining why a match is considered great.

Overtone is expected to launch later this year in select locations. Relationship expert Esther Perel and Match CEO Spencer Rascoff have joined the company's board, alongside leadership advisor Diana Chapman.
